summary:
Bingöl is a province in eastern Turkey with no documented provincial divergence from the national legal position on trans people. No province-specific ordinance, separate legal system or distinct enforcement pattern has been recorded for Bingöl, so a trans visitor here stands under the same national framework that applies across Turkey, including the draft package described below.

That framework is hostile by design. Human Rights Watch reported on 29 October 2025 on a leaked omnibus draft, the '11th Judicial Package', which would amend the Turkish penal and civil codes to criminalise behaviour it defines as 'contrary to biological sex and general morality'. Participation in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony would carry penalties of up to four years' imprisonment. The same draft would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming health care, including surgery, from 18 to 25 and attach a mandatory permanent-infertility condition, while punishing health professionals who carry out such care. Human Rights Watch called the measure one of the most alarming rollbacks of LGBT rights in decades; 15 Turkish LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association oppose it. The package had not been enacted as reported, but its drafting establishes the direction of travel for anyone assessed against Turkish authorities.

The Kaos GL 2025 report, 'A major siege against LGBTI+ people in 2025: Hostility turned into state policy', presented at its launch by lawyer Kerem Dikmen, records that anti-LGBTI+ hostility has been institutionalised as explicit state policy. Senior officials' hate speech and instructions issued to public institutions under a 'Year of the Family' banner created a climate encouraging human-rights violations, while regulatory and supervisory bodies systematically restricted freedom of expression and artistic freedom.

For a trans visitor the practical exposure points are checkpoint identity checks, in which original photo identification must be produced and compared against presentation, and any contact with police under 'General Information Gathering' (GBT) practice. Both are national patterns; the only regional-grade note specific to the east concerns security practice rather than law, namely emergency-era policing and elevated police presence.
tangentialFactors:
Bingöl sits within a province-level structure of 81 units, of which 73 carry the national score because no sub-national legal variation was found for them. The absence of a provincial rule is a finding about uniformity, not about leniency: the national measures apply here without dilution.

The eastern provinces are distinguished in reporting by security practice, not by statute. Emergency-era policing arrangements and a higher density of security personnel shape street-level contact in the region, which matters for a trans visitor because document checks and GBT stops are the moments at which passport gender markers are exposed.

The draft 11th Judicial Package is contested domestically as well as internationally: 15 Turkish LGBT organisations and the Turkish Medical Association oppose it, and Human Rights Watch issued a dedicated news release on it in October 2025. Opposition does not suspend enforcement behaviour in the interim.
localsOnly:
Residents of Bingöl are subject to the same national restrictions as the rest of Turkey. Under the leaked 11th Judicial Package, behaviour deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' would be criminalised, same-sex ceremony participation would face up to four years, and gender-affirming care eligibility would move from 18 to 25 with a permanent-infertility requirement and penalties for the treating clinicians.

Kaos GL's 2025 documentation establishes that hostility toward LGBTI+ people is administered through public institutions rather than left to individual prejudice, with a 'Year of the Family' framework driving official instructions and supervisory bodies curbing expression and artistic freedom.

Prison conditions for LGBT detainees nationally involve segregation, arbitrary searches, de facto isolation and binary administrative placement by registered sex, with complaints procedures reported as ineffective.
